win_your_money_back.name: Win Your Money Back (WYMB)
win_your_money_back.summary: Customers can earn back their investment by completing specific actions that generate results, testimonials, and upsell opportunities.

tasks.description: Create 3-5 specific, measurable actions customers must complete to 'win their money back'
Determine how much you can afford to refund based on upsell revenue projections
tasks.formula: Max Refund = (Expected Upsell Revenue × 30%) - Cost to Deliver

tasks.description: Create a checklist or dashboard to track each customer's completion progress
Choose between cash refund or store credit (store credit = 100% return for future purchase)
tasks.recommendation: Store credit recommended - creates upsell opportunity

tasks.description: Craft a compelling headline that emphasizes risk-reversal
templates: Do the work, get your money back.
Complete the challenge, win your investment back.

tasks.description: Design a clear, visual checklist customers receive at purchase
Create simple way for customers to submit their completed actions
Identify 2-3 moments during the challenge where upsells make sense
Send immediately after purchase with checklist and excitement
Encourage and remind of first milestone
Share success story + introduce upsell subtly
Celebrate completion, request testimonial, present upsell
Track: Customer name, purchase date, actions completed, completion %, refund status
Automated request for testimonial upon completion
How and when credits/refunds are issued
Track which completers purchase the upsell and when

common_mistakes: Making completion criteria too easy (no engagement = no results)
Making completion criteria too hard (no one finishes = bad reputation)
Not tracking completions properly (disputes, confusion)
Missing the upsell opportunity at completion moment
Forgetting to capture testimonials from completers
quick_wins: Start with store credit, not cash refund (100% goes back into your business)
Make first action completable within 24 hours (builds momentum)
Use completion as social proof (share stories publicly with permission)

giveaway.name: Flagship Giveaway
giveaway.summary: Use a compelling prize or scholarship to generate massive lead volume, then convert non-winners through discounts or partial scholarships.

tasks.description: Select something with high perceived value that attracts your ideal customer
tasks.key_principle: Prize must be something YOU deliver (not cash) to attract ideal customers

tasks.description: Determine actual cost to deliver vs. perceived value
tasks.formula: ROI = (Non-Winner Conversions × AOV) / (Prize Cost + Marketing Spend)

tasks.description: Ensure compliance with sweepstakes/contest laws in your jurisdiction
Simple form capturing essential info
Optional actions that give extra entries and increase engagement
Track entries, bonus entries, and referral sources
High-converting page explaining prize and entry process
How you'll select and verify the winner
Build excitement around winner reveal
Create compelling offer for everyone who didn't win
3-5 emails to convert non-winners
Confirm entry, explain prize, build excitement
Show what past winners/customers achieved
Remind about giveaway, push bonus entry actions
Announce winner, immediately present non-winner offer
Convert non-winners with special offer + deadline

common_mistakes: Giving away cash or generic prizes (attracts wrong audience)
Making entry too complicated (reduces entries)
Not having a strong non-winner offer ready
Missing legal requirements for sweepstakes
Not building anticipation before winner announcement
quick_wins: Run giveaway for 7-10 days max (urgency drives action)
Announce winner on a live stream for engagement
Use referral entries to make it viral

decoy_offer.name: Decoy Offer (Good/Better/Best)
decoy_offer.summary: Use tiered pricing where a strategically designed middle option makes the premium offer look significantly more attractive.

target_metrics.conversion_rate: Equal or higher than single offer

tasks.description: Start with your ideal offer—what you want most people to buy
Strip down version that's less attractive
tasks.principle: Remove enough value that premium looks like obvious choice

tasks.description: Price this close to premium but with significantly less value
tasks.key_principle: Decoy should be clearly worse value than premium at similar price
tasks.example: Basic: $97, Better: $197, Best: $247 (Better is the decoy)

tasks.description: Visual side-by-side showing all tiers
tasks.highlight: Premium tier with 'Most Popular' or 'Best Value' badge

tasks.description: Price tiers to make premium the obvious choice
tasks.formula: Decoy price should be 70-90% of premium price with 40-60% of value

tasks.task: Calculate value-to-price ratio for each tier
tasks.description: Premium should have highest value-to-price ratio
tasks.example: Basic: $100 value/$97, Better: $200 value/$197, Best: $500 value/$247

tasks.description: Consider testing different price points for decoy
Present all three options clearly with premium highlighted
Frame each tier appropriately

tasks.task: Add social proof to premium tier
tasks.description: Show testimonials specifically from premium customers
Introduce all three tiers with comparison chart
Case study of premium customer's transformation
Address common questions about tier differences
Urgency around premium bonuses expiring

common_mistakes: Making decoy too attractive (people actually buy it)
Pricing tiers too far apart (no anchoring effect)
Not highlighting premium tier visually
Confusing feature lists (customers can't compare easily)
Not testing different decoy prices
quick_wins: Always show premium in the middle or right position
Use visual hierarchy (larger, colored, badges) for premium

buy_x_get_y_free.name: Buy X Get Y Free
buy_x_get_y_free.summary: Value-stacking front-end offer where buying a core product includes bonus units or additional products at no extra cost.

tasks.description: Select product with good margins that people repurchase
Ensure profitability even with free units
tasks.formula: Profit = (Units Sold × Price) - (Total Units × Cost) - Marketing
tasks.example: Buy 2 Get 1 Free: Charge for 2 ($40), deliver 3 (cost $18), profit $22

tasks.description: Create attractive combination
Add time or quantity limit
Show what they're getting with crossed-out prices
Lead with the value proposition

tasks.task: Create comparison to single unit purchase
tasks.description: Show the savings vs. buying individually
Add complementary product at checkout
Convert one-time buyers to recurring
tasks.offer: Get this deal every month with Subscribe & Save (extra 10% off)

tasks.description: Offer bulk/subscription after initial purchase
tasks.timing: Immediately after purchase or in confirmation email

tasks.description: Show exactly what they're getting and the savings
Remind of limited-time nature of offer
Last call before offer expires
Offer to lock in the deal monthly

common_mistakes: Offering free units without checking margin math
No scarcity (offer runs forever, loses urgency)
Not upselling to subscription for recurring revenue
Choosing products people don't repurchase
Making the offer too complicated to understand
quick_wins: Test Buy 1 Get 1 50% Off vs Buy 2 Get 1 Free (same economics, different psychology)
Add subscription option to capture recurring revenue
Use odd numbers (Buy 3 Get 2) for higher perceived value

pay_less_now_or_pay_more_later.name: Pay Less Now or Pay More Later
pay_less_now_or_pay_more_later.summary: Time-sensitive pricing structure where early buyers get a better deal, creating urgency and rapid sales velocity.

tasks.description: This is what the offer is genuinely worth and what late buyers pay
tasks.principle: Full price must be real—not inflated for fake discounts

tasks.description: Determine discount for early action
Define when and how price increases
Add expiring bonuses for extra urgency
tasks.example: First 24 hours: Get bonus ($500 value). Day 2-3: Price stays but bonus gone.

tasks.description: Visual countdown on sales page and in emails
Clear messaging about what happens when
tasks.example: Price goes up to $997 at midnight. Save $300 by acting now.

tasks.description: Show real-time purchases or countdown of spots remaining
examples: 47 people joined in the last hour

tasks.description: Extra value only for early buyers
Additional bonus for very first buyers
tasks.example: First 10 buyers get private coaching call

tasks.description: Announce offer, explain early bird pricing, create excitement
Case study + reminder of early bird deadline
Answer objections, remind of price increase
Final warning, heavy urgency, last chance
Show price did increase (builds credibility for future launches)

common_mistakes: Fake urgency (price doesn't actually go up—destroys trust)
Too many price increase deadlines (confusing)
Not following through on deadline (never do this)
Starting with price too low (no room for future sales)
Not capturing late buyers at full price
quick_wins: Always follow through on deadlines (builds long-term trust)
Send 3 emails on deadline day: morning, afternoon, night
Show proof the price went up after deadline (screenshot, social proof)

free_with_consumption_to_upsell.name: Free With Consumption
free_with_consumption_to_upsell.summary: Offer the first session, module, or sample for free, and let the experience naturally lead into a premium upsell.

tasks.description: Select something that demonstrates your value without giving everything away
tasks.principle: Must be valuable enough to impress, limited enough to leave them wanting more

tasks.task: Ensure free offer leads to premium
tasks.description: Free experience should naturally create desire for full version
tasks.example: Free first coaching call → They realize they need ongoing support → Premium coaching

tasks.description: Know your cost per free user to ensure unit economics work
tasks.formula: Break-even = (Cost per Free User) / (Conversion Rate × Premium Price)

tasks.description: What action should they take after consuming free offer?
Make upgrading easy and natural
tasks.best_practice: Payment method already on file, one-click upgrade

tasks.description: Bonus for upgrading within time window
examples: Upgrade within 48 hours, get bonus ($X value)

tasks.task: Position upgrade at natural stopping point
tasks.description: Place upgrade offer where free content ends
tasks.example: End of free module: 'Ready for the rest? Upgrade now for...'

tasks.description: Free experience must be high-quality to convert
Design free experience to create realization of value
tasks.example: Quick win within first 15 minutes that shows this works

tasks.description: Tease premium features/content throughout free experience
Deliver free offer, set expectations, build excitement
Check in, highlight value, introduce premium option
Remind of upgrade bonus expiring

tasks.task: Day 3: Last chance for upgrade incentive
tasks.description: Final call for special upgrade offer
Continue nurturing those who didn't upgrade immediately

common_mistakes: Giving away too much (no reason to upgrade)
Free offer is low quality (poor first impression)
No clear upgrade path or call-to-action
Not following up quickly after free consumption
Missing the 48-72 hour conversion window
quick_wins: Make upgrade one-click if possible (card on file)
Follow up within 24 hours of consumption
Create urgency with expiring upgrade bonuses
